Specify a union-formation process

Source: R/union_formation.R
union_formation.Rd

Constructs a union formation process specification for a simulation model. The convenience function set_union_formation is equivalent to set_process(model, union_formation(...)) and allows for direct piping from a model.

Usage

union_formation(
  initiation,
  rates = NULL,
  matching = age_gap_matching_model(0, 5),
  father_matching = NULL,
  cohab_matching = NULL,
  cohab_prob = NULL,
  union_convert_rate = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  weights_conversion = NULL,
  min_male_age = 15,
  kinship_generations = 2,
  cancel_birth_if_no_match = TRUE,
  cohab_as_previous_union = FALSE,
  diagnostics = FALSE
)

set_union_formation(
  model,
  initiation,
  rates = NULL,
  matching = age_gap_matching_model(0, 5),
  father_matching = NULL,
  cohab_matching = NULL,
  cohab_prob = NULL,
  union_convert_rate = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  weights_conversion = NULL,
  min_male_age = 15,
  kinship_generations = 2,
  cancel_birth_if_no_match = TRUE,
  cohab_as_previous_union = FALSE,
  diagnostics = FALSE
)

Arguments

initiation

Either "on_demand" for birth-triggered searches or "rate" for scheduled searches. No default is selected.

rates

For rate mode, a nonempty data frame defining the marriage rate schedules. Must contain at least numeric age_start, age_end, and rate. See details for description of stratification variables that can be applied.

matching

A specification created by matching_model(), or a tibble with numeric time_start, time_end, and list-column model holding complete matching objects. Defaults to age_gap_matching_model(0, 5): preferred age gap zero years, with selection weight halving five years on either side.

father_matching

Optional matching specification for fathers of unpartnered births in rate mode, created by matching_model(), or a time_start/time_end/model schedule as for matching. Defaults to NULL, using the general matching model active at that birth.

cohab_matching

Optional matching model or whole-model schedule for cohabitation; NULL shares the general matching model.

cohab_prob

Optional age-specific probability table defining the probability that a union is a cohabitation. See details for specification.

union_convert_rate

Optional age- or duration-specific conversion table, defining conversion rates of cohabitations into marriages. See details for specification.

weights

NULL (default) for unweighted selection of searching women, or a weight_model() using person variables, which chooses which unpartnered woman in a cell searches without changing the cell's input search rate. Rate mode only.

weights_conversion

NULL (default) for unweighted selection, or a weight_model() using union variables, which chooses which cohabitation in a cell converts to marriage without changing the cell's input rate.

min_male_age

Minimum male age in continuous years for partner eligibility, default 15. Finite nonnegative scalar; zero disables this age exclusion.

kinship_generations

Generation bound on both sides of a known common ancestor defining partner ineligiblity, default 2. Excludes parents, grandparents, siblings, aunts/uncles, nieces/nephews and first cousins, including half relationships, when known. Zero imposes no cross-person kin exclusion. See extract_kin() for the shared distance definitions.

cancel_birth_if_no_match

Logical, default TRUE. Cancel a birth when its on-demand partner search or rate-mode nonmarital father selection fails. Set FALSE to allow births with unknown fathers. Historical missing father IDs are retained. Partner scarcity can reduce realized fertility below inputs.

cohab_as_previous_union

Logical, default FALSE. FALSE only marriage defines the previous_union value; TRUE cohabitation or marriage define the previous_union value.

diagnostics

Logical, default FALSE. When TRUE, adds additional technical variables from matching model to each union record.

model

A hammel_model object.

Value

union_formation() returns a hammel_union_formation process; set_union_formation() returns an updated model.

Details

The union formation process is female-centric. Women initiate searches and select male partners. Two different approaches to union search initiation are provided for the required initiation argument:

  • The "on_demand" approach will initiate a union search when an unpartnered woman gives birth. This approach should not be used with fertility rates that are stratified by union_type because unpartnered fertility is what creates the search. This approach is useful if the user has no particular interest in union formation processes but wants to assign parentage correctly for kinship determination.

  • The "rate" approach uses female marriage rates defined by the rates argument. The input should be a marriage rate schedule that may be stratified by group dimensions and/or previous_union. When stratified by previous_union, remarriages may be duration-specific rather than age-specific. This approach should generally be used with fertility rates that are stratified by union_type, although it is not required. Failure to stratify by union_type will lead to independence between fertility and union formation.

Once a search is initiated, a woman will select a male partner from among all eligible male partners. Men related to the women are considered ineligible out to a kinship depth defined by kinship_generations and men below min_male_age are also ineligible. the decision itself is determined by the provided matching_model which uses a conditional logit formulation to score potential suitors by age differences and group exogamy. See matching_model() for more details.

It is possible for this search to fail if no eligible men are available. When using the "on_demand" method, the cancel_birth_if_no_match argument controls whether the birth continues if no match is found. If set to FALSE, the birth continues but with NA values for the father. If set to TRUE, observed fertility rates may deviate from input rates.

When unpartnered fertility is allowed, the matching_model will also be used to identify the father of a birth to an unpartnered woman. Users can optionally specify a separate father_matching model for this case.

Cohabitation can be added to the union formation process by specifying cohab_prob and union_convert_rate. The cohab_prob argument expects a data frame that is similar to a rate process object. It contains age-specific bands defined by age_start and age_end, but also contains a prob column rather than a rate column. This prob column defines the probability that a union formed by a woman of the given age is a cohabitation instead of a marriage. Like rate processes, cohab_prob can be stratified by time period using time_start and time_end, group dimensions, or by previous_union.

The union_convert_rate is not required, but is necessary for cohabitations to be able to convert into marriages. It follows the standard rate process format and can be either duration or age dependent. It can also be stratified by time period and group dimension.

By default, partner selection for cohabitation will use the matching_model argument. Users can specify a matching model specific to cohabitations with the cohab_matching argument.

Examples

union_process <- union_formation(
  initiation = "rate",
  rates = usa_2000_marriage,
  matching = age_gap_matching_model(3, 5)
)

model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility_union) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_process(union_process)
